oauth.notes: GitHub offers OAuth apps and GitHub Apps. This guide covers OAuth apps.

verdict.summary: A self-serve form with no review. The only surprise comes later: organisations block new OAuth apps by default, so an owner must approve yours.

whoYouNeed.why: To register the app under a personal account.

whoYouNeed.role: An owner or admin of your GitHub organisation (optional)
whoYouNeed.why: Only if the app should belong to the company's organisation rather than a person.

steps.title: Sign in to GitHub
steps.plain: Log in to the GitHub account (or organisation) that should own the app.
steps.whyHuman: Signing in is yours to do. An agent can carry on once you are signed in.

sources.title: GitHub Docs: Creating an OAuth app

steps.title: Choose your callback address
steps.plain: Pick the address in your app where GitHub sends people back after they click Allow, for example https://yourapp.com/auth/github/callback. Your code receives a one-time code there and swaps it for a token.
steps.technical: GitHub calls this the Authorization callback URL. Your callback handler sends the code, client_id and client_secret to https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token. The redirect_uri your code sends must match it.

steps.title: Register the OAuth app
steps.plain: Fill in GitHub's short form: the app's name, your website, and your callback address.
steps.technical: Profile picture > Settings > Developer settings > OAuth apps > New OAuth App. Fields: Application name, Homepage URL, Application description (optional), Authorization callback URL (up to 10). Leave Enable Device Flow off unless you need a CLI flow. 'Expire user access tokens' is on by default. For an organisation-owned app use https://github.com/organizations/YOUR-ORG/settings/applications/new.

sources.title: GitHub Docs: Creating an OAuth app

link.label: Open GitHub's new OAuth app form

steps.title: Generate the client secret and store it in your app
steps.plain: On the new app's page, generate a client secret. Store it, with the client ID, in your app's secret store or environment variables, never in code.
steps.whyHuman: The secret is a password for your app. Pasting it yourself keeps it out of any agent's chat history.

evidence.note: Keeping secrets out of the agent's context is our recommendation, not a GitHub rule.

steps.title: Test a connection
steps.plain: Sign in with a test GitHub account through your app. The approval screen should show your app's name, and your callback should get a code it can swap for a token.

link.label: See or revoke apps you have authorized

nuances.title: Everything on the form is public
nuances.detail: GitHub shows the app's name, description and homepage to users. Do not put internal URLs or other private details there.
nuances.ifStuck: Edit the app under Developer settings at any time.

sources.title: GitHub Docs: Creating an OAuth app

nuances.title: A user says the app can't see their company's repositories
nuances.detail: Their organisation has OAuth app restrictions on, which is the default for new organisations.
nuances.ifStuck: Ask the user to request access from their organisation owner during the connection, or the owner can approve the app in the organisation's settings.

sources.title: GitHub Docs: OAuth app access restrictions

nuances.title: Limits
nuances.detail: One account or organisation can own up to 100 OAuth apps, and each app can have up to 10 redirect addresses.
nuances.ifStuck: Reuse one app per environment rather than one per customer.

sources.title: GitHub Docs: Creating an OAuth app

config.redirectUriNote: Your app's own callback URL, entered as the Authorization callback URL. It must match the redirect_uri your code sends.

scopes.name: repo
scopes.plain: Read and write all repositories the user can access, including private ones.

useCases.label: Read or change code, issues and pull requests
useCases.summary: No review. Users in organisations may need their org owner to approve your app.

sources.title: GitHub Docs: Creating an OAuth app

composio.note: You can connect users today with Composio's own GitHub app while yours is set up or in review. Users see 'Composio' on the consent screen, rate limits are shared with other Composio customers, and polling triggers run at most every 15 minutes. Switch to your own app when it is ready.

existingApp.summary: Reuse it. Its callback URL must match the address your agent's sign-in uses. Generate a separate client secret for the agent so you can revoke it without touching your product.

reReviewTriggers.effect: An OAuth app holds at most 10 callback URLs. Remove an unused one or register a second app.

sources.title: GitHub Docs: Creating an OAuth app

reReviewTriggers.trigger: You want a separate secret for your agent
reReviewTriggers.effect: GitHub lets you generate another client secret on the app's page; the existing one keeps working until you delete it.

evidence.note: From GitHub's app settings screen; not confirmed on a docs page we read.

reReviewTriggers.effect: No review. GitHub OAuth apps ask for scopes when the user connects, so users just see a new approval screen.

evidence.note: GitHub's scope docs were not part of this check.

blockers.symptom: Your app only sees an organisation's public repositories
blockers.cause: New GitHub organisations turn on OAuth app access restrictions by default. Until an owner approves your app, members cannot grant it access to the organisation's private data.
blockers.fix: Each user requests approval for your app when they authorise it. An organisation owner approves it under the organisation's Third-party access settings. Tell users this before they connect.

escalate.label: GitHub: how owners approve an OAuth app

sources.title: GitHub: About OAuth app access restrictions
GitHub: Approving OAuth apps for your organization

blockers.cause: The redirect address sent during sign-in does not match the callback URL registered on your OAuth app.
blockers.fix: Make the app's Authorization callback URL match the redirect_uri your code sends, then try again.

authorize.detail: Sign-in endpoint answers by asking the user to sign in first
